chunks: That it is He who makes you rich and contented;

key_terms.أَغْنَىٰ: The Enricher, one who grants wealth and abundance
key_terms.أَقْنَىٰ: The Satisfier, one who grants contentment and sufficiency

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Ghanna and Aqna in Quranic theology?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted to contrast material wealth with spiritual sufficiency, emphasizing that God alone grants both the means of enrichment and the inner contentment that renders it meaningful. The term 'Al-Aqna' specifically denotes the capacity to be satisfied with what is provided, highlighting a divine attribute of making His servants self-sufficient in spirit. This dual aspect underscores the belief that true prosperity is not merely accumulation but the divine bestowal of peace and adequacy.
